quiver: A quick, small movement back and forth.
cockleshell: The shell of a small sea animal, used here around a pond as a border.
minion: A person who does what a powerful person says, without asking why.
populace: All the people who live in a place.
portcullis: A heavy iron door that is let down in front of the way into a castle.
vizard: The front part of a metal head cover worn by a fighter, which covers the face.
halberd: A long weapon with a sharp metal end on a long stick.
flagon: A large container with a handle for drink.
keep: The strongest part of a castle, where people go to be safe.
gaoler: A man who guards the people in a prison.
murrain: An old word for a sickness of farm animals. Here it is used to wish bad things on someone.
straying: Going away from where you should be.
fascination: A strong power to hold your interest.
ford: A place where a river is not deep and you can walk or drive across.
phosphorescence: A soft light that you see in the dark, without fire.
majesty: Grand and beautiful, like a king.
moorings: The ropes that hold a boat in place.
culvert: A covered way for water to go under a road.
osier: A kind of tree that grows by water; its thin branches are used to make things by hand.
rudder: A flat piece at the back of a boat, used to turn it.
gem: Covered with small bright stones, as a ring is.
imperious: Used to having people do as it says; strong in a way that you cannot say no to.
pervading: Present in every part of a place.
eddy: A small round movement of water going round and round in a river.
sloe: A small, dark fruit that grows on a wild tree.
cowed: Made afraid, so that you do not move.
aspen: A kind of tree whose leaves move a lot in the wind.
vigil: A time of staying up at night to watch or wait.
waddle: To walk with short steps, moving from side to side, as a fat bird does.
lilting: Having a light, happy sound that goes up and down.
noisome: Having a very bad air that makes you feel ill.
hospitable: Kind to people who come to your home.
audacious: Very brave, with no fear of what people think.
lurid: Wild and strong, with bright details that make people afraid.
piebald: Having large spots of two colours, as black and white.
sulk: A time of being angry and not speaking.
coaxingly: In a soft way that tries to get someone to agree.
fragrance: A sweet, nice thing that the nose can sense.
chivalry: The brave and polite ways of soldiers on horses in old stories.
fender: A low metal guard in front of a fire.
sanitation: Ways of taking waste away from houses and keeping them clean.
avidity: A strong wish to have or do something.
sty: A small building on a farm for fat animals with short legs and a curly tail, kept for their meat.
sovereign: An old British piece of gold money.
gag: Put a cloth over someone's mouth to stop them speaking.
artifice: A clever plan to make people believe something that is not true.
untarnished: Still clean and bright; not made bad.
sally: A quick, clever thing said as a joke.
simulated: Made to look real, but not real.
wicket: A small door cut into a big door.
uncanny: Strange in a way that makes you a little afraid.
truncheon: A short thick stick carried by the police.
supplication: A very strong asking for help, with great respect.
pomp: Grand show with fine clothes and big events.
rowan: A tree with small red fruit.
peremptory: Making you do what it says at once, with no talking.
querulous: Always saying what is wrong, in a weak, unhappy voice.
shamefacedly: In a way that shows you feel bad about what you did, and look down.
beckon: To call someone to come, with a movement of the hand.
dormant: Not active now, as if sleeping.
treachery: The wrong act of turning against someone who trusts you.
eaves: The lower edges of the top of a house, where it stretches out over the wall.
canopied: Covered above by a cloth that is held up.
cistern: A big container for holding water.
gondola: A long, narrow boat with a high end, used in the water streets of Venice.
vaporous: Full of thin cloud, like water in the air.
valerian: A plant with tufts of small flower heads, which grows on old walls.
stanchion: A post or bar that stands up and holds something.
sheaf: A bunch of cut stalks of grain, held together.
lyrical: Full of feeling, like a song.
beseech: Asking in a very strong way, with great need.
toilet: The act of getting yourself clean and dressed.
heartening: Giving you hope and making you feel brave.
taut: Pulled straight and hard, with no give.
tiller: A long handle used to turn a boat.
imp: A small child who does bad things for fun.
trollop: A woman who is not clean or careful in her ways. It is an old and unkind word.
humbug: A person who says things he does not mean, to fool people.
simmer: Being heated softly, so that small bubbles come up.
mangle: A machine with two round parts that press water out of wet clothes.
rutty: Full of deep lines made in the ground by vehicles.
gorse: A wild plant with yellow flowers and sharp points.
voluptuous: Giving great happiness to the body, such as to the nose or mouth.
solace: Help and rest for someone who is sad.
cajole: To get someone to do something by saying nice things.
hackney: A horse of a good kind used for pulling light vehicles.
trappings: Fine things put on a horse to make it look grand.
rakishly: In a way that is a little wild and careless, such as a head cover worn to one side.
ignominiously: In a way that makes you look small and silly in front of others.
bankrupt: A person who has no money left and cannot pay what he must.
gaol: Prison. This is an old way to write the word.
mutinously: In a way that refuses to do what you are told.
ferret: A small, thin animal that people use to chase small animals out of holes.
paling: One of the upright pointed sticks in a line around a garden.
parapet: A low wall at the edge of a bridge or the top of a house.
portentous: Seeming to tell of something important that will come.
salon: A meeting of clever people who talk about art or ideas.
sweep: A person whose work is cleaning the place where smoke goes up from a fire.
pantry: A small room where food is kept.
murmur: A soft, low sound, or a quiet saying that you do not like something.
answerable: Being the one who must answer for it if something goes wrong.
carouse: Drinking and having fun in a noisy way with others.
brandish: Holding a weapon up and moving it in the air to show it.
bristling: Standing up straight and hard, like hair on an angry animal.
flourishing: Moving something in the air in a proud way.
debris: Broken pieces left after something is broken.
guava: A fruit that grows in hot countries.
trifle: A soft, sweet food made with fruit and a sweet milk sauce.
libel: A lie that is written or said about someone and hurts their name.
inflated: Thinking you are better than you are.
traces: The ropes that join a horse to the thing it pulls. Also: small signs that something was there.
